saying: Nearly all commenters accept the master file concept but say voluntary disclosure alone won't close gaps, asking FDA to specify minimum, versioned content—training-data cutoff, model identity and version lineage, known failure modes, subgroup evaluations, change and deprecation notification—keeping the deployed device the unit of evaluation, with sponsors holding contractual information rights. Supernova Technologies questions self-filed disclosures entirely.

disagreement.text: Commenters split on how to fix weak developer incentives: some would keep the program voluntary and confidential while shifting evidence burden or creating procurement pressure when no master file exists, while others want required disclosure, contractual disclosure duties, or a public subset of master file content.

sides.summary: Keep participation voluntary and proprietary content protected; drive disclosure through incentives, burden-shifting defaults, or a narrow public tier evaluated before any requirement.

Voluntary disclosure is inadequate; FDA should expect or require foundation-model information, mandate minimum content, add contractual duties and authority to request more, or expose a public subset.
